'''Frank Ainley Bisby''' (April 24, 1945 &ndash; October 25, 2011) was a botanist who specialized in legumes, and was a pioneer in the development of [[Taxonomy (biology)#Databases|taxonomic databases]]. He is noted for his work in founding [[Species 2000]] in 1997, which coordinated the publication of the ''[[Catalogue of Life]]'', the most comprehensive catalogue of species.<ref>''Memorandum and Articles of Association of Species 2000, 11 December 1997'' [http://documents.sp2000.org/Legal/Species2000_Memorandum&Articles.pdf] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120508192245/http://documents.sp2000.org/Legal/Species2000_Memorandum%26Articles.pdf |date=2012-05-08 }}</ref><ref>[http://iczn.org/content/obituary-frank-bisby-1945-2011 ''Obituary: Frank A. Bisby (1945-2011)'']</ref> Bisby was the first chair of the [[Taxonomic Database Working Group|Taxonomic Database Working Group (TDWG)]], which was founded in 1985. Bisby continued to lead significant projects, including the [[International Legume Database and Information Service|International Legume Database and Information Service (ILDIS)]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.tdwg.org/about-tdwg/history/ |title=''TDWG History'' |access-date=30 December 2012 |archive-date=3 August 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170803013430/http://www.tdwg.org/about-tdwg/history/ |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>[http://www.ala.org.au/blogs-news/two-biodiversity-informatics-colleagues-passed-away/ Two Biodiversity Informatics Colleagues Passed Away]</ref> He served as a professor of botany at the [[University of Reading]] for most of his career.<ref>{{Cite web|url = http://www.reading.ac.uk/news-and-events/inthenews/Media861.aspx|title = University of Reading|website = University of Reading|access-date = 2016-05-21}}</ref>

After his PhD at Oxford University he worked with the University of Southampton before becoming a professor in botany at Reading University.
